memory_candidates.content: A repository-wide generated-counts file can turn every Lean-line-adding commit into a two-step commit. In BimodalLogic, typst/generated/status.typ pins formalsystem-line-count, and a pre-commit gate (scripts/typst-sync-check.sh Check 2) BLOCKS any commit staging .lean files whose line delta the committed count no longer reflects. Its --no-verify bypass is explicitly scoped to drift caused by another writer, so it does not cover your own addition: the remedy is a full lake build, then 'bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix', then staging that file alongside your own. Consequence for plan authoring: a plan whose file_scope lists only the files its phases edit will under-declare by exactly this path, and every phase commit will collide with the gate before anyone notices the omission. Add the generated-counts file to file_scope at plan time whenever a phase adds or removes Lean lines.

When a plan's phase-1 docstring is told to describe a file that a later phase of the SAME plan creates, write it as an explicit forward reference rather than either asserting the file exists or dropping the sentence. Asserting it makes the library carry a false claim for as long as the later phases are unlanded (and a blocked plan leaves it false permanently); dropping it loses a plan-mandated disclaimer. A short parenthetical naming where it lands keeps both the disclaimer and the truth value, and the deviation is one annotated checklist line rather than an escalation.
